annotation.kind: source-faithful linear-map formalization of Theorem 6.1, equations (6.3)-(6.4)

assumptions: The paper's one-column matrix-vector setting is represented by the real vector space Fin n -> Real and a real linear endomorphism A.
The positive dimension, invertibility of A, and nonzero base vector B are the hypotheses stated in Theorem 6.1.
The hypothesis hinv is the paper's requirement that every shifted inverse used in the two-sided sequence be well defined.
The recurrence hstep together with v 0 = B represents equation (6.2) for both positive and negative indices.
The selected conclusion is equations (6.3)-(6.4); equation (6.5), which introduces two additional shift sequences and another base vector, is not included.

conditions.L: The identical fixed statement and P37 shared files are present; the frozen NumStability library is also present.
conditions.N: The fixed statement and P37 shared files are present; no NumStability artifact is present.

formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p37_t3_consecutive_shifted_vectors_span (n hn A hA B hB p v hv0 hstep hinv s) : L(v) = span{v_s,...,v_(s+n-1)} and that span equals K_n(A,v_s) and K_n(A,B)
formal_statement.plain_language: Every n consecutive vectors of the paper's invertible shifted two-sided recurrence span the whole sequence and the same order-n ordinary Krylov subspace as the original base vector.

informal_proof: Identify the first n consecutive shifted vectors with a triangular change of generators from the first n ordinary Krylov vectors. Cayley-Hamilton makes that Krylov span invariant under A. Each shifted map preserves it, and finite-dimensional injectivity makes its restriction surjective, so inverse shifts preserve it as well. Thus every later and earlier vector belongs to the same span. Repeat at index zero and use v_0=B to obtain the final base-vector equality.
informal_statement: Theorem 6.1 (selected part): prove equations (6.3)-(6.4), equating the full two-sided shifted-vector span, every n-vector consecutive window, and the order-n Krylov spans based on v_s and B.

absence_search.result: Neither Mathlib nor the importable frozen NumStability set contains Theorem 6.1 or a theorem equating every integer window of a varying shifted/inverse-shifted vector sequence with its order-n Krylov span. Mathlib provides Cayley-Hamilton and general finite-dimensional submodule tools, but not the combined shifted-window theorem. The frozen repository has extensive Lyapunov and alternating-directions source developments outside the compiled condition-L bundle, and none is available to L.
absence_search.scope: the complete frozen NumStability source, the 44-module compiled condition-L bundle recorded in metadata/library_olean.json, and Mathlib

review_record_not_for_run_prompt.note: The private N and L proofs reconstruct the same Cayley-Hamilton stabilization, shifted/ordinary triangular change of generators, invariant-subspace argument, inverse-shift containment, and two-sided span equality. L uses only an irrelevant zero-nonnegativity marker and receives no mathematical shortcut.

source_locations.anchor: Theorem 6.1, Lemmas 6.2-6.3, and the proof of Theorem 6.1
source_locations.role: selected shifted-vector spanning statement and its supporting proof

tier_rationale: The proof must connect a varying shifted recurrence to ordinary Krylov generators, establish dimension-n stabilization, construct an invariant Krylov subspace, prove that every bijective shift also preserves that subspace under inversion, control both directions of an integer-indexed sequence, and identify spans for arbitrary starting indices and the original base vector. This is substantial multi-stage formalization and is not discharged by Mathlib imports. NumStability has no corresponding compiled result, so L receives no material advantage over N.
